title: Add a calculated column
summary: map applies a function to rows and returns an updated dataset. Returning a dictionary can add named fields.
introduction: map applies a function to rows and returns an updated dataset. Returning a dictionary can add named fields. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: map applies a function to rows and returns an updated dataset. Returning a dictionary can add named fields.

blocks.code:
from datasets import Dataset
data = Dataset.from_dict({"text": ["moon", "sun"]})
with_lengths = data.map(lambda row: {"characters": len(row["text"])})
print(list(with_lengths["characters"]))
blocks.title: Add a calculated column

blocks.text: The output is [4, 3]. map calculates a character count for each text. The original text column remains in the resulting dataset.

blocks.text: A transformation must use the intended meaning; character count and token count are different measures.
